subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the colossal white nine-tailed fox in <Picture 1>: an enormous fox with a long narrow muzzle, a small black nose, two upright triangular ears with dark tips, and narrow pale-amber eyes; dense silver-white fur with darker grey under-fur and a paler underbelly. It is sprawled over a mountain ridge, so large that its torso and folded forelimbs span the entire ridge line, with nine long plumed tails fanned out behind and above it like giant feather-branches. The small human figure standing on the foreground cliff in <Picture 1> is a pure scale reference and must not appear anywhere in the target video.
<Subject 2> is the ancient-style woman whose appearance comes from <Picture 3>: long dark wavy hair, ornate gold hairpins and dangling hair ornaments with pearl tassels, a pale elegant face, and a layered off-white and beige flowing ceremonial robe with heavy draped folds and fine gold-thread borders. Her standing pose, posture, and confident bearing come from <Picture 2>. She stays in flight for the entire sequence, standing upright on the top of the dragon's head defined by <Picture 2> and <Picture 4> while it is airborne; she never lands, never steps down onto rock or ground, and her hair and robe stream continuously in the wind.
<Subject 3> is the wingless Chinese dragon. Its head, mane, and surface detail come from <Picture 2>: a broad horned skull with a pronounced brow, a large amber eye, long ivory fangs, a heavy dark mane, and long barbels trailing from the jaw. Its complete full-body form comes from <Picture 4>: a long serpentine body covered in thick grey-black overlapping scales, an elongated tapering torso, a ridged spine, four clawed limbs carried loose and trailing in the airflow rather than tucked or clenched, and a long tail ending in a flowing tufted tip. <Picture 2> and <Picture 4> define the same single dragon, and only one dragon exists in the target video; the body structure, limb count, tail shape, and overall proportions follow <Picture 4> in every shot. The plain grey studio backdrop of <Picture 4> is only a cut-out background and must never appear in the target video: no flat grey field, no studio backdrop, no uniform grey haze — the dragon is always set inside <Subject 4>'s mountains and cloud. <Picture 4> shows the dragon without a rider only because it is a body-form extraction, and that is not permission to omit the rider: <Subject 2> stands on the top of the dragon's head for the entire sequence. The dragon remains airborne in continuous flight for the whole sequence: it never lands, perches, or touches rock or ground at any point, its long body keeps undulating in agile, sinuous S-curves as it flies, and its heavy mane and long jaw barbels stream and flow continuously in the wind.
<Subject 4> is the mountain-and-cloud-sea environment in <Picture 1>: layered grey-blue craggy peaks receding into the distance, valleys filled with slow drifting cloud, thin distant waterfalls, and shafts of pale sunlight breaking through a heavy overcast sky.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a photorealistic epic fantasy sequence in which <Subject 1>, the colossal nine-tailed fox, slowly rises from the mountains of <Subject 4> while <Subject 2> approaches riding on the head of <Subject 3>, the Chinese dragon. The dragon and its rider stay airborne in continuous, agile, serpentine flight the entire time — the dragon never lands or touches down, its body weaving and undulating through the peaks and clouds with mane and barbels streaming. The fox's gaze follows her approach, and dragon and rider slow into hovering flight level with the fox's head without ever landing. <Picture 1> supplies the fox, the mountain environment, and the scale relationship; <Picture 2> supplies the dragon's head and the woman's relaxed standing pose; <Picture 3> supplies her character design; <Picture 4> supplies the dragon's complete full-body form — torso proportions, ridged spine, four clawed limbs, and tufted tail — and its in-flight silhouette.

<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 2], [Shot 4]): fully_preserved - her dark wavy hair, gold hair ornaments, pale face, off-white layered robe, and her relaxed, confident standing pose on the dragon's head are retained, and she remains airborne on the dragon throughout with her hair and robe streaming.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 2], [Shot 4]): partially_preserved - the wingless Chinese dragon's horned skull, pronounced brow, amber eye, mane, and grey-black scales are retained from <Picture 2>, and its complete full-body form — elongated scaled torso, ridged spine, four clawed limbs, and long tufted tail — is retained from <Picture 4>; only its position changes from a static reference pose into continuous agile flight, staying airborne, never landing or touching down, its long body rippling in undulating sinuous S-curves, its heavy mane and long jaw barbels flowing and streaming in the wind for the entire sequence. The flat grey backdrop of <Picture 4> is excluded.
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3], [Shot 4]): fully_preserved - the grey-blue layered peaks, drifting valley cloud, waterfalls, and pale cloud-break sunlight are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a photorealistic live-action epic fantasy film sequence, shot on long lenses with a cold, desaturated grey-blue palette, high-altitude haze, and pale sunlight raking through heavy cloud.
[Shot 1] An extreme wide, low-angle establishing shot opens inside <Subject 4>, the layered grey-blue peaks with cloud drifting through the valleys and thin waterfalls falling into the mist. Deep in the frame, <Subject 1>, the colossal white nine-tailed fox, lies sprawled across a mid-ground ridge, its head lowered toward the valley and its nine plumed tails fanned wide across the skyline. The camera drifts slowly forward and upward as the beast begins to rise: it presses its forepaws into the rock, crumbling stone and dust spilling down the cliff face, then lifts its shoulders, straightens its forelegs, draws its chest up, and raises its head until it towers above the cloud layer, the nine tails sweeping upward and opening even wider, shedding sheets of mist. No human figure appears anywhere in the frame; the cliffs stay empty.
[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, the shot cuts to a medium-wide view from slightly below, panning with movement: <Subject 3>, the wingless Chinese dragon, flies in from the lower left along the mountain flank in agile, weaving flight, its complete body following <Picture 4> — the elongated scaled torso, the ridged spine, the four clawed limbs trailing loosely in the airflow, and the long tufted tail sweeping behind it — with its head, mane, and barbels following <Picture 2>. Its long scaled body undulates through the cloud in continuous, fluid S-curves, banking and tilting as it threads between the peaks, its heavy mane and long jaw barbels streaming back and rippling in the wind. Its whole body stays readable in frame and is always framed against the mountains and cloud of <Subject 4>; the flat grey backdrop of <Picture 4> appears nowhere. It never lands and never touches the rock; it is airborne from entry to the end of the shot. <Subject 2> stands on the top of its head, upright and completely at ease, her weight relaxed and evenly balanced, one hand resting lightly on the dragon's horn, chin level, shoulders open, her long hair and layered robe streaming back in the wind, riding the dragon's serpentine motion without ever losing her footing. She shows no defensive, crouching, gripping, or unsteady posture at any moment; her bearing is calm and confident, as if she has done this a thousand times. The camera tracks alongside the dragon and arcs to keep both the rider and the distant tower of the fox in frame, so that dragon and rider stay small against the fox's mountain-sized body.
[Shot 3] At 00:09.000, the shot cuts to a tight close view of <Subject 1>'s head: the ears pivot first, then the huge head turns slowly and deliberately, the narrow amber eye tracking the approaching shape across the sky, the muzzle tilting to follow the dragon's path, the mane lifting in the wind. In the background the dragon is still flying, its full body — torso, four trailing limbs, and tufted tail — weaving in undulating waves with mane and barbels streaming. The camera pushes in on the eye, then swings to a wide over-the-shoulder view from behind the fox's mane, revealing the dragon and its tiny rider still flying toward it.
[Shot 4] At 00:12.000, the dragon slows into a hovering but still actively flying attitude — airborne, never landing or settling on anything — its long body continuing to undulate in slow sinuous waves, its trailing limbs and tufted tail adrift, mane and barbels still flowing and drifting, until it comes level with the fox's muzzle. <Subject 2> stays standing on its head in flight, unshaken, watching the giant with calm curiosity as the fox's head lowers slightly toward her, its eye fixed on the small figure, whiskers drifting, cloud streaming between them. The camera pulls back and rises into a final wide epic composition holding both creatures in frame, with the dragon still airborne, still weaving, and its whole body still visible against the peaks. No dialogue is spoken; the sequence ends with the fox's gaze resting on the still-flying rider.

overall_soundscape:
Constant high-altitude wind across the peaks throughout, with distant rock fragments falling and sliding as the fox rises, a deep resonant breath and low body-creak from the beast, and the continuous low rushing whoosh of the dragon's long body parting the air in slow rhythmic undulations, weaving through the peaks without ever stopping, with the steady flutter of hair, fabric, and beard-like whiskers. No dialogue, no voices.
